sources.title: Alberto Bressan, Hyperbolic Conservation Laws: An Illustrated Tutorial (81-page lecture notes)
sources.locator: Complete 81-page PDF; read §§2.2–2.3, printed pp. 13–15, and §§3.3–3.4, printed pp. 24–29. Bressan explicitly leaves technical details mostly out; all proof obligations below are supplied locally.

contents.name: §2.2: construction of local shock curves from an augmented Rankine–Hugoniot equation
§2.3: Lax admissibility inequalities
§3.3: characteristic integral curves and centered rarefaction waves
§3.3: Rankine–Hugoniot shocks, rarefactions, and linearly-degenerate contacts
§3.3: shock and rarefaction curves have a common tangent at the base state
contents.reason: The source gives the tangent statement; the local carrier proves the augmented IFT system and the first-order speed expansion needed for the Lax sign.

contents.name: §3.4: ordered composition of elementary waves and invertibility of the wave-strength map
§3.4: uniqueness of small wave strengths for nearby left/right states

sources.title: Randall J. LeVeque, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws (complete 228-page book)

contents.name: Ch. 6 §6.5: eigenvector decomposition of a linear-system Riemann jump
Ch. 7 §7.1: weak jumps and the Hugoniot locus
Ch. 7 §7.2: local solution of the nonlinear system Riemann problem
Ch. 7 §7.2.1: large-data Riemann problems with no entropy solution of the stated elementary-wave form
contents.reason: The assigned general-system theorem is explicitly local near one strictly hyperbolic state; arbitrary large-data existence is excluded by the controlling design.

contents.name: Ch. 7 §§7.3–7.5: genuine nonlinearity, Lax shocks, and linear degeneracy
Ch. 7 §7.6: local Riemann construction from elementary waves
Ch. 8 §§8.1–8.3: integral curves, rarefaction fans, and general local solution
Ch. 8 §8.4: collisions of multiple waves after a Riemann interaction
contents.reason: Wave interaction after the initial self-similar Riemann fan is a separate evolution problem and is not part of the approved PE01 scope.

contents.name: Ch. 9 §9.1: linearly-degenerate Euler contact discontinuity
Ch. 9 §9.2: Euler Riemann solution reduced to a scalar pressure equation, including vacuum discussion
Ch. 13 §13.2: Godunov interface flux from the local Riemann trace
Ch. 14 §14.2: Roe matrix jump identity and numerical flux
Ch. 14 §14.2.2: a sonic entropy fix for the Roe solver
contents.reason: The approved scope requires the expansion-shock failure condition and does not add a modified entropy-fix solver; the false entropy implication is refuted locally.

sources.title: David I. Ketcheson, Randall J. LeVeque, and Mauricio J. del Razo, Riemann Problems and Jupyter Solutions, Part II
sources.locator: Complete HTML chapter, 555 extracted lines; read the Roe solver and entropy-fix sections at lines 15–23 and 155–170 and the HLL solver derivation/implementation at lines 365–427.

contents.name: Part II, shallow-water Roe solver: real averaged matrix, exact flux-jump identity, and eigenwave decomposition
contents.reason: The source illustrates the general Roe matrix interface in a different system; the local definition states the abstract hypotheses and the local counterexample proves the Burgers entropy failure.

contents.name: Part II, Roe entropy fix: splitting a transonic rarefaction to avoid an entropy-violating discontinuity
contents.reason: An entropy-corrected Roe variant is outside the approved scope; the original Roe flux's failure is retained as a fully proved Burgers counterexample.

contents.name: Part II, HLL fictitious two-wave solution and conservation equation for the middle state
Part II, lower and upper wave-speed bounds and shallow-water HLLE estimate
contents.reason: The specific Einfeldt speed estimate is shallow-water dependent; the HLL definition makes enclosing speeds an explicit hypothesis and proves no unverified general bound.

contents.name: Part II, shallow-water HLL positivity and isolated-shock exactness claims
contents.reason: These properties belong to a different shallow-water solver and are not asserted for the general systems or ideal-gas Euler states in this pair.
